question:
(i) Explain how electrical power is dissipated in a resistor when current flows through it.
(ii) A junction diode is used as a half-wave rectifier with a load resistor. Explain how power is delivered to the load only during one half-cycle of the input AC.

options.A:
(i) A resistor converts electrical energy into heat. The power dissipated is $P=VI=I^2R=\dfrac{V^2}{R}$.
(ii) In a half-wave rectifier, the diode conducts in its forward-biased half-cycle, allowing current and power delivery to the load. In reverse bias it offers high resistance, so current and load power are nearly zero.
options.B:
(i) A resistor stores electrical energy without dissipation, and $P=\dfrac{I}{R}$.
(ii) A half-wave rectifier diode conducts equally in both half-cycles, so equal power is delivered throughout the cycle.
options.C:
(i) Electrical power in a resistor is $P=IR^2$ and does not depend on voltage.
(ii) The diode delivers power only when reverse biased and blocks the forward-biased half-cycle.
options.D:
(i) A resistor converts heat energy into electrical energy and $P=\dfrac{R}{I^2}$.
(ii) The diode produces AC at the load during the non-conducting half-cycle.
